author: Mark Magnier
description:
A senior Russian aide suggested on Tuesday that Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin could hold a trilateral meeting at the next Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Leaders of the 21-member grouping are scheduled to meet in Shenzhen, the Chinese economic powerhouse in southern China, on November 18 and 19, setting up the possibility of Xi and Trump meeting four times this year.
Asked on Russian state television about ⁠the...
title: Xi, Trump and Putin may hold trilateral meeting at next Apec forum, Kremlin says

author: Han Li
description:
US lawmakers are trying to identify which foreign countries are the biggest sources of unlawful robocalls targeting Americans, as Congress steps up efforts to combat a surge in phone scams.
The inquiry follows a string of US government reports tying much of the financial damage from scams to Chinese criminal networks based in Southeast Asia.
The House Energy and Commerce Committee’s Communications and Technology Subcommittee passed the bipartisan “Foreign Robocall Elimination Act” on Tuesday,...
title: US Congress seeks to identify foreign countries behind scam calls

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s defence ministry has warned that the People’s Liberation Army is stepping up its preparations for a blockade of the island, adding that it is sharpening its plans to break such a cordon in response.
The assessment was made in the ministry’s “2026 China Military Power Report”, which was submitted to the legislature this week along with its five-year force development plan and next year’s proposed defence budget.
The report said recent PLA exercises were increasingly focused on the “joint...
title: Mainland China stepping up preparations for Taiwan blockade, report says

author: Vincent Chow,Lucy Quaggin
description:
The US Congress on Tuesday advanced a new bill that seeks to establish American global leadership in open-source artificial intelligence, an area where China currently dominates, by promoting adoption of US open-source models and publicising risks associated with using their Chinese counterparts.
The legislation was one of several proposals marked up in the US House of Representatives targeting China amid escalating tech competition between the two countries.
Congressional committees “mark up” a...
title: Congress advances new bill to give US edge in open-source AI race with China

author: Mark Magnier
description:
US President Donald Trump launched new air strikes on Iran on Tuesday, the latest chapter as the president has swung in recent weeks between economic and military pressure tactics, all the while claiming that Tehran was on its heels.
US Military Central Command announced on social media that the attacks were in response to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’s recent attempted attacks on commercial ships in the strategic Strait of ‌Hormuz and against American service ‌members deployed ‌to the...
title: US military carries out new strikes on Iranian targets as hostilities flare

author: Mark Magnier
description:
The latest trade war between the United States and Canada marks a turning point with key lessons for China and other major US trading partners as well as risks, say analysts and former trade officials, as US President Donald Trump continues to put his blunt stamp on global institutions.
The breakdown in ties between Washington and Ottawa, one of the largest trade relationships in the world, opens one more front in the president’s disruptive path that could fuel a backlash and further distrust to...
title: China, global trading partners watch closely as Trump takes on Canada

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Not even the world’s fastest sprinters could have outrun the devastating floodwaters that struck a border crossing between China and Nepal last week, according to one of the first peer-reviewed assessments of the disaster.
Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calculated that the surface velocity of the debris flow was 19 metres per second (62 feet per second) when it struck the checkpoint at Gyirong Port in Tibet.
This is almost twice Usain Bolt’s average speed when he set the...
title: China-Nepal floods: first research shows that no one could have outrun debris flow

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven of the most interesting and important news stories covering global relations from the past few weeks. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Trump says he plans to meet Kim Jong-un this year, citing good relationship

US President Donald Trump said that he planned to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un later this year, despite Pyongyang denying that the two leaders were in direct communication.
Read the full story here.
2. China...
title: Trump’s North Korea hope, US revokes visas, China’s rocket force: 7 global relations reads

author: Victoria Bela
description:
As Starship, the world’s largest and most powerful rocket, gears up for an attempt to finally reach Earth’s orbit, experts say the risk of an in-flight catastrophe – and a cloud of debris – “needs to be of concern”.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX is expected to launch the Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy booster for the launch system’s 14th test flight and first orbital test flight later this month.
According to one aerospace expert, if the Starship’s upper stage explodes in orbit it could produce debris...
title: Starship could create more debris than an anti-satellite test if it explodes in orbit

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China has demanded protection of its interests in Venezuela after a US-backed energy company was granted 100-year concessions covering oilfields previously operated by Chinese and Russian firms.
“China-Venezuela cooperation is protected by international law and the laws of both countries. China’s legitimate rights and interests in Venezuela must be guaranteed,” foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said in Beijing on Tuesday.
“Economic and trade cooperation between countries should follow the...
title: China demands rights guarantee as US firm secures 100-year Venezuelan oil deal

author: Alex Lo
description:
Michael Pettis says a great rebalancing is coming and China will pay for it. It’s strange how the man who insists that power decides who pays never tests his claim on Washington. The Beijing-based economist has been warning that a great rebalancing is coming since he published a book called The Great Rebalancing. That was in 2013.
His latest Foreign Affairs offering? You guessed it: “A Great Rebalancing Is Coming: Who Will Bear the Costs of a Global Trade Adjustment?”
It’s the same plot: Today’s...
title: If a ‘great rebalancing’ is coming, will China really have to pay for it?

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
In a rare display of interoperability, a Chinese YY-20 aerial tanker has been pictured refuelling a French-built Egyptian Rafale fighter – showing a versatility analysts say could enable closer multinational air operations and improve the tanker’s potential for export.
The photo, released by the Egyptian military on Monday, showed mid-air refuelling during the Eagles of Civilisation 2026 joint exercise, which began last month and is being held at several airbases across Egypt.
The YY-20, also...
title: Export potential? Chinese YY-20 refuels Egyptian Rafale in cross-platform drill

author: Orange Wang
description:
US Senator Steve Daines, a close ally of President Donald Trump, has wrapped up a days-long trip to China, weeks ahead of Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s planned visit to Washington.
According to a Chinese local government and multiple corporate accounts, the Montana Republican travelled from Wednesday to Saturday to China’s tech hub Hangzhou and the southern city of Guangzhou.
The visit is consistent with an earlier South China Morning Post report about Daines’ return trip to China.
Those reports...
title: Trump envoy Daines visits Chinese AI, space firms to lay groundwork for Xi summit in US

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Residents and rescuers in the Tibet autonomous region paused for three minutes on Tuesday morning to remember the victims of last week’s mudslide disaster.
Sirens sounded for three minutes from 9.55am at the Gyirong Port police station, with similar memorials at rescue and road-reopening sites throughout the region, according to state broadcaster CCTV.
More than 1,000 people died and thousands remain missing along the China-Nepal border area after a glacier collapsed at Langtang Lirung on the...
title: Glacier risk hangs over China-Nepal border as region remembers mudslide victims

author: Holly Chik
description:
Award-winning Swedish chip expert Henry Homayoun Radamson has died in Shanghai at the age of 63.
Radamson, who moved to China in 2016, was working as the chief scientist at the Guangdong Greater Bay Area Institute of Integrated Circuit and System.
The institute said on Tuesday that he died from a “sudden illness” on August 12.
In 2023, Radamson was awarded the Chinese Government Friendship Award, which recognises those who have made outstanding contributions to China’s development.
He was best...
title: Swedish chip expert Henry Homayoun Radamson dies in China of ‘sudden illness’, aged 63

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China has made the first amendment in 16 years to its national defence mobilisation law to include a fresh focus on new technologies – a move experts said would cover AI and drones.
Analysts said the inclusion would make it possible to rapidly convert emerging infrastructure, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and unmanned systems, into defence capabilities.
The revised law, passed by the top legislature on Friday, says that “the state promotes the application of advanced technologies in...
title: China highlights advanced wartime tech in defence mobilisation law update

author: Andy Xie
description: The US threat of sanctions on China because of Beijing’s relationship with Iran isn’t credible. The artificial intelligence bubble and its own precarious bond market make the US more vulnerable to a shock than China. Even if the US risks massive self-harm and kicks major Chinese institutions off SWIFT, the global messaging system enabling dollar-based cross-border payments, it will merely accelerate the yuan’s rise. China’s trading partners can easily switch to the perfectly functional yuan...
title: Why US sanctions threats against China aren’t credible

author: SCMP Reporter
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called on world leaders to create an environment of “universal security”, and firmly prevent external forces from interfering in the internal affairs of other countries.
At the 10-member Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Tuesday, Xi said the grouping should safeguard regional stability.
He called the Eurasian security bloc a “new type of regional cooperation organisation with the largest geographical area, the largest...
title: Xi raises ‘universal security’ mission for SCO as Putin, Modi meet in Kyrgyzstan

author: Meredith Chen
description:
Parts of eastern and southern China are bracing for heavy to torrential rain over the next three days, with authorities warning of floods, landslides and mudslides, as Typhoon Saudel re-forms over the South China Sea.
Several airports could be affected, including Guangzhou Baiyun, Shenzhen Baoan, Zhuhai Jinwan, Xiamen Gaoqi, Fuzhou Changle, Wenzhou Longwan, Ningbo Lishe and Hong Kong International Airport, according to aviation data platform VariFlight.
So far, no large-scale flight...
title: ‘Unprecedented’ path: eastern and southern China braces for revived Typhoon Saudel

author: Chao Kong
description:
Modern simplified Chinese characters form a tightly connected network from just 514 basic components that evolved through a process similar to natural selection, according to researchers who say their findings could change how Chinese writing is taught.
“Chinese characters evolve like living organisms,” lecturer Xie Yonghui of Shanghai Normal University said on August 24.
The research into the evolution of Chinese writing over thousands of years, led by Huang Wei, of Beijing Language and Culture...
title: Chinese script evolved like a living organism driven by natural selection: study

author: Junjie Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping ended August in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, kick-starting a potential run of overseas trips after what has so far been a quiet year for foreign travel.
Xi met Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov ahead of a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. He may hold talks with other SCO attendees including Russia’s Vladimir Putin and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian. After the summit, the Chinese president will fly to Egypt, where he will meet President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. The...
title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker, August 2026

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
A prominent American university has agreed to pay a US$2.1 million settlement to resolve allegations that it failed to disclose employees’ ties to China when applying for federal grant funding, the Department of Justice announced on Monday.
Ohio State University’s (OSU) settlement relates to Nasa and National Science Foundation (NSF) grants that provided funding to the university from November 2012 to August 2023.
Both Nasa and the NSF required the public university to disclose “foreign...
title: US university to pay US$2.1 million settlement over claims it didn’t disclose China ties

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
A false espionage alarm about a Taipei subway user has fuelled concerns that growing fears of Beijing are breeding unhealthy suspicion on the island and eroding public trust.
The controversy erupted after a social media user posted a photograph of a man holding a laptop on a Taipei Main Station metro platform on Saturday.
Seeing the words “2nd Theatre Photosynthesis System” appeared in simplified Chinese on the laptop’s screen, the social media user suspected that the man was a mainland Chinese...
title: The laptop, the social media user and the false alarm in Taiwan over a Beijing ‘spy’
